title: The Terminal of the Rust Belt Revisited
premise: Rosalind Okonkwo pilots the freighter Long Memory along a decaying trade loop between colonies that have severed contact with Earth, carrying cryo-preserved backup copies of colonists whose originals died in an incident no one will name. When children across three colonies begin dreaming the same dream—a burning settlement, a locked vault of erased records—Rosalind realizes the backups in her hold are the only surviving witnesses. To prove the Kettle Creek massacre happened, she must wake the backups, an act forbidden by the charter she swore to uphold and by the man she loves, charter auditor Elias Vann, whose career depends on the official silence. In the end Rosalind broadcasts the backups' testimony to every world on the loop, sacrificing her ship and her clean record, and chooses exile with Elias and the woken dead rather than the safety of forgetting.
about_author: Wendell Delacroix is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent nine years routing cargo through shrinking industrial corridors before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep systems running after the systems have stopped caring about them.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Rosalind navigates the Long Memory through a dead-relay corridor, establishing her routine, her bond with engineer Tam Osei, and the sealed hold she never opens. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: weary competence masking dread; she counts the backups like a rosary and tells no one why.

chapters.title: Charter and Chain
chapters.summary: At Meridian Station, charter auditor Elias Vann boards to inspect cargo manifests. Rosalind and Elias share a careful, years-long intimacy neither will name, since his duty is to report exactly the thing she hides. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: love conducted as bureaucratic ritual, tenderness hidden inside procedure.

chapters.title: The Dream Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: In the colony of New Anvil, eight-year-old Binta Ferreira draws the same burning settlement forty other children have drawn. Her teacher, Maren, sends the images to the colonial net; within hours the drawings are deleted by an automated filter. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: unease curdling into fear as adults realize the children share a memory no living person has.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Rosalind finds one backup pod cycling warm, its occupant's vitals flickering as if dreaming in tandem with the children. She runs diagnostics she is not authorized to run. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into purpose; the hold is no longer a tomb but a witness box.

chapters.title: Audit of Ash
chapters.summary: Elias cross-references Kettle Creek and finds a settlement charter issued and rescinded in the same week, eleven years ago, with all associated records purged. His supervisor orders him to close the file. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: the auditor's faith in the charter cracks; duty and truth pull apart for the first time.

chapters.title: Children of the Smoke
chapters.summary: The dreams spread to a second colony. Maren organizes the children's drawings into a single composite image of Kettle Creek's layout, including a vault beneath the chapel no map shows. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: found family forming among the frightened; adults choosing the children over their own safety.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Rosalind wakes Adaeze's backup for ninety seconds—enough for Adaeze to say 'we burned' before Rosalind shuts the pod down, shaking. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: grief and revelation entwined; her sister was at Kettle Creek, and Rosalind's navigation logs from that year are the missing record.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signs Silence
chapters.summary: Elias confronts his mentor, Director Ilsa Reyes, who admits the massacre was real and was erased to keep the colonies from seceding. She offers him promotion and complicity. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: seduction of power against the pull of conscience; he takes the offer and hates himself.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Rosalind learns of the deletion order through a smuggler's data leak. She and Tam plot a route that will let her broadcast from the old Kettle Creek relay before the deletion executes. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: found family solidifying—Tam, who never knew what the hold held, chooses Rosalind and the dead without hesitation.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Dead
chapters.summary: Elias, auditing Rosalind's ship, finds the backup manifest and understands everything. Rosalind, expecting arrest, instead watches him quietly amend the record to buy her time. POV: alternating Rosalind/Elias. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal—he chooses her over the charter in ink before he can say it aloud.

chapters.title: The Composite
chapters.summary: Maren's composite drawing reaches Rosalind via the colonial net's last unfiltered node; it matches Adaeze's ninety seconds of testimony exactly, including the vault. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: the children's shared dream becomes evidence; hope that memory itself can testify when records won't.

chapters.title: Exclusion Zone
chapters.summary: The Long Memory crosses into the exclusion zone; colonial cutters shadow them but hold fire while cameras watch. Rosalind navigates the dead relay field on instinct and Adaeze's fragmentary memories. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into clarity; the route she once flew to forget becomes the route she flies to remember.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: A maintenance 'inspection' team boards at a fuel stop and plants a fault in the broadcast array. Tam finds it with hours to spare but is injured defusing it. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing a side; the crew is no longer invisible, and invisibility was their armor.

chapters.title: Reyes Descends
chapters.summary: Director Reyes arrives at New Anvil personally, charming the colonists while ordering Maren's quiet transfer offworld. Elias, assigned as her aide, must decide whether to warn Maren. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: duty's last stand—he tips off Maren with a routing code, burning his career in a single keystroke.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Chapel
chapters.summary: Guided by the children's composite, Rosalind and Tam land and open the buried Kettle Creek vault: physical records, bone fragments, and a hand-carved memorial the erasure missed. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: proof made flesh; grief finally has an address.

chapters.title: Wake the Dead
chapters.summary: Rosalind begins waking the backups in sequence to record testimony, against every law and her own fear. Adaeze, awake for real now, forgives her sister for running. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: reconciliation with the dead; the hold becomes a courtroom, the ship a sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: From the Kettle Creek relay, Rosalind transmits the vault evidence, the children's composite, and 214 testimonies to every world on the loop. Colonial networks try to filter it; the children, dreaming in unison, recite the names aloud in their classrooms until the filters fail. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: climax—the dead speak, and this time everyone listens.

chapters.title: Fire on the Relay
chapters.summary: The Long Memory takes weapons fire covering the broadcast's final minutes. Tam holds the array together while Rosalind flies the ship through its own burning signal path. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: sacrifice without martyrdom—they survive, but the ship that was their home does not.

chapters.title: Hearing of the Loop
chapters.summary: Colonial assemblies convene; the evidence is undeniable. Reyes's network collapses as subordinates confess to save themselves. Elias testifies, formally ending his charter career. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: justice that arrives without triumph; the record is corrected, but nothing erased can be restored.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Rosalind, Adaeze, Tam, Maren, and the children gather in the vault-turned-memorial. Rosalind finally mourns openly, and the found family that formed across the route becomes a household. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: grief integrated; memory kept by choice, not by secrecy.

chapters.title: A New Route
chapters.summary: The crew signs onto a smaller ship, the Adaeze, running an honest route between colonies that now speak to one another. Elias, stripped of office, signs on as cargo clerk—the lowest rank, the freest man. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: love no longer against duty, because they have written a new duty together.

chapters.title: The Terminal of the Rust Belt
chapters.summary: At the loop's oldest terminal, Rosalind installs a permanent broadcast beacon playing the 214 names on loop. Adaeze stands beside her as the beacon lights. POV: Rosalind, closing. Emotional beat: resolution—what was hidden is now a lighthouse; the dead are not cargo but compass.
